sources.news_title: Romo on leave from CBS Sports after arrest on suspicion of OWI
sources.text:
Tony Romo has been placed on leave from his role as the lead analyst on CBS’ NFL coverage following his arrest last week on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.
CBS Sports announced Friday that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was on leave “until further notice.” JJ Watt will join Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson as CBS Sports’ lead NFL team during Romo’s absence.
Romo, 46, was arrested July 23 after he was stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 in Wisconsin. According to the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office report, Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests before getting taken into custody, booked and released.
He has a court date set for Sept. 21.
CBS Sports’ announcement comes after citations released by the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office indicated an open bottle of an alcoholic beverage was found in the passenger’s side of Romo’s black Jeep during an inventory before it was towed.
According to the citations, police stopped Romo after he was seen passing cars in a gore area, which separates interstate traffic from cars entering from an on-ramp. Police said Romo questioned what a gore area was during the stop.
Body camera footage released earlier this week showed Romo telling deputies he had been coming from a golf course and was on his way “to visit grandma and grandpa” when he was stopped. A deputy told Romo he suspected him of being impaired because he had “red glassy eyes” and an “odor of an intoxicating alcoholic beverage.”
Romo went to high school about 35 miles from Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin.
He has been the lead game analyst for CBS’ NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.
Romo remains the Cowboys’ franchise leader in career touchdown passes with 248. He held the franchise record for career passing yards (34,183) until Dak Prescott overtook him last season.
Watt joined CBS in 2023. He was an analyst on “The NFL Today” for two seasons before teaming with Ian Eagle on the network’s No. 2 crew beginning last season.
Romo wasn’t expected to have his first game until the opening Sunday of the regular season on Sept. 13. CBS will air a preseason game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles on Aug. 28.
CBS likely will reveal its game assignments and announcer pairings for the first three weeks of the regular season in the next couple of weeks.

sources.news_title: CBS Benches Tony Romo After Wisconsin OWI Arrest - American Liberty News
sources.text:
Former NFL quarterback Tony Romo has been pulled from CBS Sports’ top broadcast booth following his arrest on suspicion of impaired driving in Wisconsin.
“Tony Romo is on leave from his role at CBS Sports until further notice,” a network spokesperson told Page Six.
The abrupt decision comes less than two months before the NFL regular season and leaves one of television’s most prominent — and highly paid — sports broadcasters fighting for his future at the network.
Traffic Stop Caught On Camera
Romo, 46, was stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 in Milwaukee on July 23 after deputies allegedly observed him passing vehicles through a restricted gore area, according to the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office.
Body-camera footage released by authorities showed Romo telling a deputy that he was returning from a golf tournament and traveling to visit family.
When the deputy said she suspected he might be impaired, Romo denied drinking and repeatedly asked to contact his attorney.
“I’ll do it, but I’m not allowed to call my lawyer first?” Romo asked when told to complete a field sobriety test.
“Because I’m coming from a golf course, you think I’m drunk?” he asked later.
At the county jail, a deputy told Romo that authorities had noticed his “red glassy eyes” and an “odor of an intoxicating alcoholic beverage,” according to ABC News.
The deputy also said several small liquor bottles — commonly called “shooters” — had been discovered in his vehicle.
Romo completed portions of the field sobriety testing but refused a preliminary breath test.
“We’re not doing that,” Romo said in the footage. “I’ve heard from all the lawyers, ‘Don’t ever do that.’”
He also declined a blood test and was subsequently arrested on suspicion of operating while intoxicated.
Open Bottle Allegedly Found
Authorities issued Romo citations for first-offense OWI, unsafe passing and possessing an open container in a moving vehicle.
A deputy reported discovering an “open bottle of an alcoholic beverage” on the passenger side while inventorying Romo’s Jeep before it was towed, ABC News reported.
The Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office said Romo performed poorly during the standardized field sobriety tests. He was booked that evening and released at approximately 11 p.m.
Romo had not been formally charged as of Wednesday and is scheduled to appear in court on Sept. 21. A first-offense OWI is generally treated as a civil violation rather than a criminal offense under Wisconsin law.
Neither Romo nor his representatives has publicly addressed the arrest.
NFL Star Takes Romo’s Seat
CBS Sports announced that former Houston Texans star J.J. Watt will replace Romo alongside play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson on the network’s lead NFL broadcast team.
Watt, a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, joined CBS in 2023 and moved into the network’s No. 2 broadcast booth last season.
Romo entered broadcasting immediately after retiring from the Dallas Cowboys in 2017 and quickly became CBS Sports’ lead NFL analyst. His ability to predict plays before they unfolded made him an early fan favorite and eventually helped him secure a reported 10-year, $180 million contract.
Now, with CBS saying his leave will continue “until further notice,” Romo’s sudden absence has handed Watt one of the most coveted seats in sports broadcasting — and raised fresh questions about whether the former Cowboys quarterback will get it back.

Tony Romo, CBS at a breaking point after leave: ‘Worst contract in media history’
When CBS Sports signed Tony Romo to a 10-year, $180 million contract in 2020, a top sports media executive called me immediately after and said, “This is the worst contract in media history.”
It may end up being just that.
CBS has called a timeout on the deal after Romo’s arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. Following the arrest has been a steady drip of new information, including 45 minutes’ worth of multi-angle video of the traffic stop during which Romo is given a citation for an open container of alcohol that contradicted him saying he had no drinks.
The incident led the network to announce that Romo “is on leave from his role at CBS until further notice.” CBS elevated J.J. Watt to team with Jim Nantz in the network’s No. 1 NFL booth and offered no further comment.
Romo’s contract calls for him to receive a nearly implausible $72 million over the next four years, but he is going to have to make quite a case to get his top job back.
It’s not impossible, but it is going to take some work.
CBS clearly does not want the cloud from this story to shade its most important property. In less than two weeks, it has its NFL seminar for on-air talent and production staff, which includes a session in front of the media. Romo was supposed to be there.
On Sept. 13, the first Sunday of the NFL regular season, the network’s showcase game matches the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers. Romo was supposed to be there.
On Sept. 21, Romo now has a scheduled court date in Wisconsin.
On Sept. 27, CBS’ late-afternoon marquee game is from Brazil between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens. Romo was supposed to be there.
Right now, CBS doesn’t want Romo any of these places.
If he misses the first month of the season, when does he return? How does he return? With CBS slated to air a Super Bowl in February 2028, would he have a chance then? His poor performance in recent seasons is a factor here.
Romo comes across as a very affable guy and many have described him to me over the years as a “big kid.” But he is not known as a hard worker, and it has shown on the air.
Prior to his massive new deal, Nantz and Romo were welcoming comparisons to Pat Summerall and John Madden. Since then, the duo has regressed and Romo often sounded unprepared, saying odd things.
Last January, the higher-seeded Jacksonville Jaguars were at home to face the Buffalo Bills in the wild-card round, and Romo appeared on the pregame show. When the camera found him, he said of the Jaguars, “I’m telling you, they can win this game today.” The remark drew almost immediate scorn on social media for its vacuity because, of course, the higher seed with home-field advantage team could win.
The Bills needed a late touchdown from Josh Allen to be victorious, but that’s not the point.
Like all on-air TV contracts, Romo’s deal includes a morals clause, one that networks can challenge if a star is unable to represent their brand in a positive fashion after a public embarrassment.
If Romo were still working at a Madden-like level, his case to keep his job would be stronger. Since he was already trending the wrong way, he has some work to do.
Networks build their marketing campaigns around their top crews. If every time Romo says something off, there is a GIF referring to a portion of his arrest video, is that a problem for CBS?
Could he return on the No. 2 crew with Ian Eagle or could CBS tell him he has to go even further down the lineup, perhaps to convince him to walk away? Appearing in the studio could become an option, but that might be too out front for CBS.
Six years ago, one of the reasons CBS Sports chairman Sean McManus and president David Berson signed Romo to the crazy contract right before the pandemic was because ESPN was in hot pursuit. Before ESPN eventually landed Joe Buck and Troy Aikman from Fox, its “Monday Night Football” booths were consistently a hot mess.
In 2020, CBS outbid ESPN in part because the overall negotiation for rights to the game packages was about to begin. At that time, prior to COVID, there was some thought inside Disney to potentially not only keep “Monday Night Football” on ESPN, but also to go after CBS’ Sunday afternoon package for ABC. Going into the negotiation with Romo on CBS’ side instead of on Disney’s roster was considered a boon to the Tiffany Network.
Now? Not so much.
That is why we are here, staring at what might be the worst contract in sports media TV history. Romo could still make a comeback, but he is going to have to put in a lot of work, both off- and on-air.
But if he is not welcomed back, there is no way he is going to just give up the $72 million he is owed. Romo’s deal may indeed end up the worst in sports media history.
At this point, he and CBS are both going to need quite a comeback to avoid that fate.

“The Tony Romo thing is pretty cut and dry, you know what it is, you know what he did, you know that it’s regretful for sure. CBS hasn’t made any statement and I don’t suspect that they will,” Esiason told co-host Gregg Giannotti on their WFAN morning show this week. “And I think Tony will ultimately have to face questions and he’s gonna end up having to go before a judge in September right in the beginning of the football season. He’s a good guy, made a really bad, regretful decision.”
“Thank God nobody got hurt, and thank God he didn’t get hurt, and hopefully everything’s gonna be okay and he’ll learn from what is an obvious, just really bad mistake.”
It’s worth noting, Esiason made the comment about not suspecting CBS to issue a statement on Romo while his WFAN radio show was being simulcast on CBS Sports Network.
Romo currently has a court date set for Monday, Sept. 21. A first-offense OWI in Wisconsin is typically treated as a civil violation rather than a criminal charge. Romo will not have to appear in court, which should allow him to call his Week 2 game the previous day as scheduled.
The recent legal issue continues a downward trend for Romo’s TV career, who was widely praised for his broadcasting style when he entered the booth for CBS in 2017. Romo was quickly dubbed “Romostradamus” for his ability to predict plays, and soon received an industry-altering $180 million contract to remain with CBS as their lead NFL analyst.
In recent years, however, Romo has been widely criticized for mistakes, uttering strange noises and talking over broadcast partner Jim Nantz. Previous leadership at CBS even held what was described as an “intervention” with Romo in 2023 to better his preparation habits.
Some have speculated whether CBS could use the arrest as an excuse to part ways with their lead NFL analyst. But even though Romo has regressed in the booth, he maintains an immense level of fame as a former Cowboys quarterback. And as long as Nantz wants to continue working with Romo, CBS seems unlikely to make any drastic change. A statement on Romo’s arrest, however, is probably warranted.

sources.news_title: CBS Makes Decision on Tony Romo's Future Following Viral Arrest Video
sources.text:
Tony Romo’s future at CBS Sports has taken a significant turn following his recent arrest in Wisconsin.
The network confirmed Friday that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback has been placed on leave in the wake of his alleged operating while intoxicated (OWI) arrest, putting his broadcasting duties on hold indefinitely.
The decision comes just over a week after video of Romo’s traffic stop began circulating online, generating widespread attention across the sports world.
CBS Confirms Romo’s Leave
In a statement provided to Page Six, CBS Sports confirmed that Romo will not be working while the situation plays out.
“Tony Romo is on leave from his role at CBS Sports until further notice,” a network representative said.
CBS did not provide additional details regarding the length of the leave or whether Romo is expected to return for the upcoming NFL season.
RELATED: Newly Released Tony Romo Arrest Video Has Everyone Talking
Romo Has Not Publicly Addressed the Arrest
As of Friday, Romo has not made any public comments regarding the incident.
His representatives have also remained silent, declining to respond to multiple media requests for comment as attention surrounding the case continues to grow.
The lack of a public statement has only increased speculation about when—or if—the longtime broadcaster will address the situation.
Traffic Stop Led to Arrest
According to authorities, Romo was pulled over by a Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office deputy after allegedly making an unsafe passing maneuver while driving southbound on Interstate 43 over Milwaukee’s high-rise bridge.
The traffic stop ultimately resulted in Romo being arrested on suspicion of operating while intoxicated.
Body camera footage from the stop was later released, bringing even more scrutiny to the high-profile case.
One of CBS’ Biggest Stars
Romo joined CBS Sports immediately after retiring from the NFL in 2017 following a standout career with the Dallas Cowboys.
He quickly became one of the most recognizable voices in sports broadcasting, earning praise for his ability to break down plays before they happened and serving as CBS’s lead NFL game analyst alongside its top play-by-play team.
His absence would leave a significant hole in the network’s NFL coverage if the leave extends into the regular season.

TMSPN Take
Tony Romo is one of the biggest names in sports broadcasting, making this an incredibly high-profile situation. Given the attention surrounding the arrest and the release of the body camera footage, CBS likely felt it had little choice but to place him on leave while the legal process unfolds. The next chapter will depend on how the case progresses and whether Romo addresses the incident publicly.

sources.news_title: Romo On Leave From CBS Sports After Arrest On Suspicion Of Operating Vehicle Under The Influence – 710am KURV
sources.text:
Tony Romo has been placed on leave from his role as the lead analyst on CBS’ NFL coverage following his arrest last week on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.
CBS Sports announced Friday that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was on leave “until further notice.” JJ Watt will join Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson as CBS Sports’ lead NFL team during Romo’s absence.
Romo, 46, was arrested July 23 after he was stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 in Wisconsin. According to the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office report, Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests before getting taken into custody, booked and released.
He has a court date set for Sept. 21.
CBS Sports’ announcement comes after citations released by the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office indicated an open bottle of an alcoholic beverage was found in the passenger’s side of Romo’s black Jeep during an inventory before it was towed.
According to the citations, police stopped Romo after he was seen passing cars in a gore area, which separates interstate traffic from cars entering from an on-ramp. Police said Romo questioned what a gore area was during the stop.
Body camera footage released earlier this week showed Romo telling deputies he had been coming from a golf course and was on his way “to visit grandma and grandpa” when he was stopped. A deputy told Romo he suspected him of being impaired because he had “red glassy eyes” and an “odor of an intoxicating alcoholic beverage.”
Romo went to high school about 35 miles from Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin.
He has been the lead game analyst for CBS’ NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.
Romo remains the Cowboys’ franchise leader in career touchdown passes with 248. He held the franchise record for career passing yards (34,183) until Dak Prescott overtook him last season.
Watt joined CBS in 2023. He was an analyst on “The NFL Today” for two seasons before teaming with Ian Eagle on the network’s No. 2 crew beginning last season.
Romo wasn’t expected to have his first game until the opening Sunday of the regular season on Sept. 13. CBS will air a preseason game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles on Aug. 28.
CBS likely will reveal its game assignments and announcer pairings for the first three weeks of the regular season in the next couple of weeks.

sources.news_title: CBS Places Tony Romo on Leave After OWI Arrest
sources.text:
Eight days after he was arrested for OWI (operating while under the influence), CBS has placed No. 1 game analyst Tony Romo on indefinite leave.
“Tony Romo is on leave from his role at CBS Sports until further notice,” the network said in a statement on Friday.
The former Cowboys quarterback was poised to enter his 10th season on CBS’s top NFL broadcast team with play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson. But on July 23, he was pulled over by police in his home state of Wisconsin and charged with OWI. According to a police report, Romo failed field sobriety tests.
TMZ posted police bodycam footage of Romo being arrested and declining to take a breathalyzer test. Police also found an open container of alcohol in his vehicle, according to the Associated Press. The 46-year-old Romo has yet to publicly comment on the incident, while CBS had stayed silent until Friday.
JJ Watt, who debuted as a game analyst on CBS’s No. 2 team last season, will work with Nantz and Wolfson on the No. 1 team in Romo’s absence.
Romo joined CBS in 2017 after 13 seasons wth the Cowboys. He quickly became a sports media sensation, earning the nickname “Romostradamus” for his uncanny ability to predict plays before they happened. He reset the market for talent salaries by earning a 10-year, $180 million contract extension in 2020.
But Romo has taken increasing criticism in recent years due to on-air miscues and a perceived lack of work ethic. CBS could potentially save $72 million from the last four years of his contract if it uses his arrest as a trigger to terminate his deal.
Should CBS ultimately opt to move on from Romo, Watt—who earned plenty of praise calling games alongside Ian Eagle last season—would be the most obvious full-time replacement as the network’s No. 1 game analyst. CBS said on Friday that it will announce its full talent roster for the 2026 NFL season at a later date.

sources.news_title: Tony Romo on indefinite leave from CBS, JJ Watt to replace him
sources.text:
CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo is on indefinite leave from the network after his arrest last week.
CBS issued a statement Friday morning saying that Romo, its lead NFL analyst since 2017, is on leave from his role “until further notice,” and then followed that up by announcing JJ Watt as his replacement on the network’s lead NFL team with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson.
The announcement came one week after Romo was arrested for OWI in Wisconsin (the equivalent to a DUI).
CBS begins its regular season NFL coverage September 13, meaning Romo could be ‘on leave’ for a full six weeks and not miss any assignments. (The network has a preseason game August 28, but it is highly unlikely there were any plans to Romo and Nantz on that broadcast.) The fact that Watt has been named as his replacement is a clear indication that Romo’s leave will extend beyond the six-week mark.
After TNT NBA analyst Charles Barkley was arrested for DUI in December 2008, the network suspended him more than a month, with his return not occurring until after the NBA’s All-Star Weekend in February 2009. Two years later, ESPN NBA analyst Jalen Rose was taken off air while dealing with the aftermath of his own DUI arrest.
When then-NBC play-by-play voice Al Michaels was arrested for DUI in 2013, he did not miss any assignments — but his arrest occurred in April, early in the NFL offseason, and he eventually pled down to a charge of reckless driving.
Romo is at an inflection point in his broadcasting career. He went straight from his NFL playing career to becoming the lead voice of CBS NFL coverage — replacing long-time analyst Phil Simms — and had one of the most acclaimed rookie campaigns in the history of sportscasting. His knack for predicting plays, paired with his energy and enthusiasm, quickly elevated him into the position of highest-profile analyst in the sport. When it came time to renew his contract, he reset the market with a reported $17 million/year contract that was a record at the time (since surpassed).
But as time has gone on, Romo has become the target of criticism as the characteristics that were once fresh and new have gone stale. CBS last year promoted Watt to its secondary broadcast booth, a move seen as potentially paving the way for a succession plan — an unusual move given that Romo, at just 46, could easily be in the broadcast booth another 20 years.
